fields.Name: IT121 - SubQ Snap and Mercury Decide Decision Models
fields.Description: Subquadratic's SubQ Snap and Inception's Mercury Decide resolve from the synced metadata through AIDecisionRunner to the request each route would send, with no network. SM1 the Subquadratic and Inception Labs vendors take API Key credentials; SubQ Snap is an Active Decision model at PowerRank 43 with a Subquadratic Model Developer row and an Active Subquadratic Inference Provider row naming SubQDecision and subq-snap-preview with no input-token limit, and an active Realtime cost row at $0.05 per million input tokens with free output; Mercury Decide is an Active Decision model at PowerRank 44 with an Inception Labs Model Developer row, an Active Inception Labs Inference Provider row naming InceptionDecision and mercury-decide with no input-token limit, at a higher priority than an Active OpenRouter Inference Provider row naming OpenRouterDecision and the pinned inception/mercury-decide-20260930 with 65,536 input tokens, and an active Realtime cost row on each vendor at $0.02 per million input tokens with free output; both models' effective Decision limits are 255 Choice options and 10 Score levels and nothing else. SM2 the shipped SubQDecision and InceptionDecision are registered under their keys, and ClassFactory.CreateInstance builds subclasses of them (the bundle's guards) that read an API Key credential's endpoint; the default endpoints are https://api.subq.ai/v1/systemone and https://api.inceptionlabs.ai/v1/decisions. SM3 a real AIDecisionRunner.ExecuteDecision on the Default Decision prompt with override naming SubQ Snap on Subquadratic and a legacy key POSTs the System One body {model: subq-snap-preview, state, questions: noul, choice, score} for SubQ's documented example to https://api.subq.ai/v1/systemone with the key as the bearer; SubQ's documented response comes back mapped (Score probabilities read by level index and keyed by level name); and the MJ: AI Prompt Runs row is recorded against the model and Subquadratic, successful, with 477 input tokens and a cost from the cost row. SM4 the same for Mercury Decide on Inception Labs with Inception's documented example: InceptionDecision POSTs {model: mercury-decide, …} to https://api.inceptionlabs.ai/v1/decisions, OpenRouter gets nothing, and the run has 120 input tokens priced from the Inception cost row. SM5 the same override on OpenRouter builds OpenRouterDecision, which POSTs the body with model inception/mercury-decide-20260930 to https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions, and the run is recorded against OpenRouter, priced from its cost row. SM6 real API Key credentials created through CredentialEngine and bound to SubQ Snap's and Mercury Decide's Inference Provider rows (each model also has a Model Developer row on that vendor) send Authorization: Bearer <token>, not the credential's JSON, and the answers map. SM7 on a test prompt bound to SubQ Snap, then Mercury Decide on Inception Labs, SubQ answers HTTP 422 with a detail object whose message names no validation word; the attempt fails as a ModelError that allows failover, and Mercury Decide answers; with the override naming Mercury Decide and keys for both routes, Inception answers its documented HTTP 402, the attempt fails as NoCredit and allows failover, and the OpenRouter row answers. SM8 Default Decision's candidates are Jev on OpenRouter, then LLM Decision, then every existing power-matched fallback, then the new models' rows last: Mercury Decide on Inception Labs, Mercury Decide on OpenRouter, SubQ Snap; the runner selects the first of Jev and LLM Decision it has a credential for; with API Key credentials bound to both new models' direct rows they are credentialed, the order is the same and the selection does not change; and with every other decision driver made unavailable the run fails over past the credentialed candidates ahead of it, LLM Decision included, to Mercury Decide on Inception Labs (the decision drivers are the shared scripted stand-in for this check). SubQDecision, InceptionDecision and OpenRouterDecision are replaced for the whole bundle by subclasses that override only SendRequest, record each request and answer only while a check arms them, refusing with a 500 otherwise, so nothing reaches api.subq.ai, api.inceptionlabs.ai or openrouter.ai. Every prompt run, test prompt, credential, binding and credential audit-log row the bundle creates is deleted. IT121 is a provisional number and may be renumbered at merge.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: SubQ Snap and Mercury Decide are usable as Decision models: their metadata resolves with their routes, drivers, API names, prices and documented limits, SubQDecision and InceptionDecision build through the ClassFactory, and an AIDecisionRunner call naming each model and vendor row sends that route's request, maps its answers and records the run against the model and vendor; bound credentials send their tokens, SubQ's 422 and Inception's 402 fail over, and Default Decision's order is unchanged with the new models last.
